source.author: lucan
source.text: Euganeo, si vera fides memorantibus, augur Colle sedens, Aponus terris ubi fumifer exit, Atque Antenorei dispergitur unda Timavi, Venit summa dies, geritur res maxima, dixit: Impia concurrunt Pompeii et Caesaris arma; Seu tonitrus ac tela Iovis praesaga notavit, Aethera seu totum discordi obsistere coelo Prospexitque polos: seu lumen in aethere moestum Solis in obscuro pugnam pallore notavit.
source.text_original: Euganeo, si vera fides memorantibus, augur / Colle sedens, Aponus terris ubi fumifer exit, / Atque Antenorei dispergitur unda Timavi, / Venit summa dies, geritur res maxima, dixit: / Impia concurrunt Pompeii et Caesaris arma; / Seu tonitrus ac tela Iovis praesaga notavit, / Aethera seu totum discordi obsistere coelo / Prospexitque polos: seu lumen in aethere moestum / Solis in obscuro pugnam pallore notavit.
source.text_english: To the Euganean, if credence may be given to those who tell it, an augur seated on the hill, where Aponus, smoke-bearing, issues from the earth, and where the waters of Antenor’s Timavus are scattered abroad, said, The last day has come, the greatest matter is being decided: the impious arms of Pompey and Caesar are meeting; whether he had marked thunder and Jupiter’s weapons as presages, or had looked out and seen all the sky opposing a hostile heaven and the poles; or whether he had noticed in the darkened air the sad light of the sun, a pale omen of battle.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: accelerat sed summa dies Asiamque labantem linquimus et poscunt iam me sua tempora Grai.
reuse.text_original: accelerat sed summa dies Asiamque labantem / linquimus et poscunt iam me sua tempora Grai.
reuse.text_english: He hastens on, but the last day is near, and we leave Asia in its decline, and now the Greeks claim their own time from me.
